correctness.rationale: On the standard geodesic circle, the reflection has degree -1. A homeomorphism fixing a nondegenerate arc pointwise cannot be orientation reversing, so it has degree +1. Uniform distance below pi gives a continuous shortest-geodesic homotopy, forcing equal degree and yielding a contradiction. Independently, substituting the local reflection into formula (4.3) gives g_0(theta)=(1-2 rho(|theta|))theta; continuity of rho forces rho=1/2 at an intermediate radius and hence noninjectivity. The quantified boundary is exact for the argument: any epsilon strictly below pi suffices.

value.rationale: The obstruction targets a central local perturbation lemma used to pass from arbitrary finite-entropy homeomorphisms to systems with a sink in the paper's C0-density proof. It is not a cosmetic normalization: it identifies a homotopy-component barrier that any valid replacement must respect, and it supplies an explicit one-dimensional counterexample to the unrestricted lemma while carefully withholding any claim that the paper's final density theorem is false.
